dossier.public_summary: The 0.66-day dip is on the target star but repeats at exactly the star's rotation period with a very large brightness sway much bigger than the dip. The transit is much too long for this tiny M dwarf and its apparent depth changes by a factor of 10 between sectors as the star's spots change. Together this is best explained as stellar variability / eclipsing signal from the active star, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Starlight modulation at the dip period is larger than the transit depth and highly significant, classic for synchronous spotted rotation / close binary, not a planet.
Dip period is identical to the spot period measured in every sector (0.332 d alias also seen), with huge spot amplitude; a true USP planet would not have the same large rotational signal.
reasons.value: rotation_d=0.664 signal_period_d=0.664741 signal_over_rotation=1.0011159638554217 phase_curve amplitude 11789-17164 ppm vs transit 2389-5836 ppm

reasons.why: Duration is far too long for the 0.189 Rsun M dwarf and the transit density is much lower than stellar density; flat bottom (v_sigma=-2.845) alone cannot overcome this without an eccentric EB/sync geometry.
Depth changes by a factor ~10 across campaigns, correlated with sector depth, characteristic of detrending a highly variable spotted star rather than a stable achromatic planet.
reasons.value: p_constant=1.813e-24 depth_change_pct=691.3 sectors 47-50,85 depths 661-23855 ppm vs refit 2898,530,400

reasons.why: Centroid is on target and rules out neighbours, so the on-target variability is astrophysical stellar variability (spot modulation) not a blend, supporting an EB/spot origin over a planet blend.
